title: Review: Superposition, interference and coherence; Experimental methods and practical skills; Young's double slit; Diffraction grating
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W06-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W07-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MS06-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W06-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS06-1#N.4, W06-uk1#N.10, W07-1#N.2, W09-1#N.6, MS06-1#N.13, W07-1#N.9a, W09-1#N.8a, MS06-1#N.12, W07-1#N.6a, W09-1#N.10, W09-1#N.4a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Laser
items.clue: Source giving a narrow, intense beam of coherent light; ideal for interference.

items.label: Diffraction
items.clue: Spreading out of light as it leaves each narrow opening, so the two beams overlap.

items.label: Systematic error
items.clue: Kind of fault that repeating readings does not cure: change or correct the method instead.

items.label: Antiphase
items.clue: Relation between two sources that adds π everywhere, turning every maximum into a minimum.

questions.stem: On a pair of vernier callipers, the vernier's zero lies between the 31 mm and 32 mm marks of the main scale. Vernier mark 6 lines up exactly with a main-scale mark. What is the reading?

options.text: 37 mm

questions.explanation: Main scale up to the vernier's zero: 31 mm. Vernier mark 6 lines up: 6 × 0.1 mm = 0.6 mm. Reading = 31.6 mm.

questions.stem: Two loudspeakers, driven in phase by the same signal generator, face a line along which a microphone is moved. Starting from the central maximum of loudness, the microphone is moved along the line to the third maximum away from the centre. At that point its distances from the two speakers differ by 0.60 m. What is the wavelength of the sound?
Predict first. Monochromatic light passes through two very narrow slits and falls on a distant screen, producing a pattern of bright and dark bands. Which explanation accounts for this pattern?

options.text: Light travels straight through the slits, and each bright band is an image of a slit.
Light spreads out from each slit, and the waves from the two slits overlap and interfere.
Light is refracted at the edges of each slit, which bends it into separate bright bands.
Waves from the two slits interfere where they meet, so no spreading at the slits is needed.

questions.stem: Predict first. Monochromatic light is incident normally first on a double slit and then on a diffraction grating whose adjacent slits have the same separation d as the double slit. Every slit is equally illuminated. Compared with the double-slit fringes, how do the grating's principal maxima appear?

options.text: Farther apart than the fringes, because the grating has many more slits
At the same angles, but wider and dimmer, as the light is shared among more slits
Identical in position, width and brightness, because only d and λ matter
At the same angles as the double-slit fringes, but much sharper and brighter

questions.stem: A student has a ruler with 1 mm divisions and wants the thickness of one sheet of paper, about 0.1 mm. Which choice and reason are both correct?

options.text: Measure one sheet ten times and average, because averaging reduces the uncertainty.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because the reading uncertainty is shared out.
Measure a stack of 10 sheets ten times and average, because more readings always help.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because any calibration error in the ruler then cancels.

questions.stem: Laser light passes through two slits 0.25 mm apart onto a wall 2.50 m away. A student measures across six fringe spacings: the fringes span 39.0 mm. What is the wavelength of the light?
questions.explanation: Fringe spacing = 39.0 mm ÷ 6 = 6.5 mm. λ = slit separation × fringe spacing ÷ slits-to-screen distance = (0.25 × 10⁻³ × 6.5 × 10⁻³)/2.50 = 6.5 × 10⁻⁷ m: red light.

questions.stem: Predict first. White light is incident normally on a diffraction grating. Which describes the pattern seen on a screen?

options.text: A white central maximum, with a spectrum in each order on either side and violet nearest the centre
A white central maximum, with a spectrum in each order on either side and red nearest the centre
A spectrum at the centre, as well as in each order on either side, with violet nearest to the centre
A white central maximum and a white maximum in each order, as all colours share the same angles

questions.stem: A student investigates how the time t for a ball to fall from rest depends on the drop height h. (h = ½gt², with g constant.) Which plan is best?

options.text: Drop the ball once from each of three heights, timing by hand; plot t against h.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t².
Drop a ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically, with a heavier ball for the greater heights.

questions.explanation: Enough values, repeats, no reaction time, and h = (g/2)t² gives a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2.

questions.stem: In a Young's double-slit experiment, monochromatic red light is incident normally on the slits and the fringe separation on the screen is 2.0 mm. Which single change would make the fringe separation 4.0 mm?

options.text: Doubling the distance between the centres of the slits
Using blue light, of shorter wavelength, in place of the red
Halving the width of each slit, keeping their separation
Halving the distance between the centres of the two slits

questions.stem: A laser beam is directed normally at a grating with 500 lines per mm. On a screen 1.00 m from the grating, the two second-order spots are 1.50 m apart. What is the wavelength of the laser light?

options.text: 750 nm
600 nm
832 nm

questions.stem: Light of wavelength 650 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating that has 600 lines per millimetre. At what angle to the straight-through direction is the second-order maximum observed?
